summary.plain: In 2005 the STAR collaboration published a critical assessment of the first three years of RHIC nucleus-nucleus collisions. Its comparison with theory suggests that central gold-gold collisions produce dense, rapidly thermalizing matter with nearly ideal fluid flow, but the collaboration states that the measurements themselves do not yet establish unequivocal evidence for a transition to a quark-gluon plasma.
summary.technical: STAR's 2005 critical assessment (Nucl. Phys. A 757, 102-183) reviews the most important results of the first three years of RHIC nucleus-nucleus collisions, with emphasis on STAR, and compares them with theory. The comparison suggests that central Au+Au collisions produce dense, rapidly thermalizing matter with (1) initial energy densities above the lattice-QCD critical values for QGP formation, (2) nearly ideal fluid flow, established most probably before hadron formation, and (3) opacity to jets. The collaboration states that the measurements themselves do not yet establish unequivocal evidence for a transition to this new form of matter, and it poses open questions and suggests additional measurements.

title: Experimental and Theoretical Challenges in the Search for the Quark Gluon Plasma: The STAR Collaboration's Critical Assessment of the Evidence from RHIC Collisions
why_it_matters: A critical assessment by the STAR Collaboration of the RHIC evidence for a quark-gluon plasma: it says many of the observations are consistent with models incorporating QGP formation in the early collision stages and have not found ready explanation in a hadronic framework, but that the measurements themselves do not yet establish unequivocal evidence for a transition, and it lists open questions and additional measurements needed to conclude definitively that thermalized, deconfined quark-gluon matter has been produced.
